name: Mijamin
overview: Mijamin was a male descendant of Parosh mentioned in the book of Ezra. He is specifically noted for having married a foreign wife, a detail that highlights the challenges faced by the returning exiles in maintaining covenant purity. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Mijamin means 'from the right hand,' a proper name recorded in Ezra 10:25. This meaning may reflect a position of strength or favor, though the text does not explicitly assign such significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Mijamin as a descendant of Parosh, establishing a clear familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning Mijamin.
scriptureSignificance: Mijamin's mention in Ezra 10:25 serves as a representation of the broader issue of intermarriage among the returned exiles, which was addressed to preserve the purity of Israel's covenant community. His inclusion in the list underscores the communal effort to correct these breaches and maintain faithfulness to God's commands during the post-exilic restoration.
